issues.description: set_pixel (function) inconsistent write address between solution and main/problem statement: In solution_repository/pixel.asm the subroutine set_pixel computes the pixel address and executes an extra 'add eax, 4' before writing the RGB value (writing to display_start + x*4 + 7680*y + 4). In solution_repository/pixel.asm (main) the code that reads the pixel computes the address as display_start + x*4 + 7680*y (no +4) and reads from that address. The problem statement (Hausaufgabe 3, Teilaufgabe b) requires set_pixel to set the pixel at the computed address (display_start + x*4 + 7680*y). This mismatch causes main to read a different memory cell than the one set by set_pixel, producing incorrect behavior and confusing students about where pixels are written.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the extra 'add eax, 4' in the solution subroutine set_pixel so the write target matches the address computed and read by main (display_start + x*4 + 7680*y). Ensure the subroutine still preserves registers as required by the problem statement (only eax may be left modified); compute the address and perform 'mov [eax], ecx' without the +4 offset.
